attacks.claim: The public Recent signers panel renders the full name and full postal code of every confirmed signer. This violates the agreed rule that public signer lists show at most first name, last initial and city, and exposes EU signers' personal data under GDPR. Publication is hard to undo.
attacks.evidence:
• {{ s.full_name }} {{ s.city }} {{ s.postal_code }}
    • vs. 'showing first name + last initial and city'

attacks.claim: The newsletter opt-in checkbox is pre-checked. GDPR requires affirmative, unambiguous consent for marketing contact, and organizer exports and campaign news depend on this consent.

The sign form has no privacy notice or lawful-basis text, and no retention period is stated for confirmed signatures (only unconfirmed ones are purged after 7 days). The artifact also describes no erasure path for EU signers. The agreed GDPR requirement is not evidenced.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: privacy notice / lawful-basis text on sign form; ABSENT: retention period for confirmed signatures

attacks.claim: WCAG 2.1 AA is not met for the error flow. Invalid fields are marked only by a colour change, nothing writes text into the aria-live .form-error region, and there is no aria-invalid or aria-describedby. The form uses novalidate, so screen reader users get no error message.
attacks.evidence:
form.elements[fields[0]].classList.add('is-invalid') ...

— ABSENT: code that populates .form-error; ABSENT: aria-invalid/aria-describedby

attacks.claim: The accessibility evidence is insufficient. The only check is an automated axe scan of the sign page. It does not cover the error state, the Recent signers panel, or the live-updating counts, so it does not support the agreed WCAG 2.1 AA commitment for public flows.
attacks.evidence: | axe-core automated scan on sign page | 0 violations |

attacks.claim: The client handles only 422 and ok responses. A 409 duplicate, a 5xx, or a network failure leaves the user with a form that silently does nothing. The duplicate path was tested server-side only.
attacks.evidence: if (res.status === 422) {...} if (res.ok) window.location = ...; Duplicate signature (same email) rejected with 409 | Pass

attacks.claim: The rollback plan covers only the form swap. It says nothing about signer data already collected or displayed, such as unconfirmed signatures awaiting purge, pending confirmation links, or personal data already exposed publicly. Flipping the flag does not undo an exposure.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: flip `petitions_signing` off; sign form is replaced by the existing "Follow this petition" button.

attacks.claim: Rollout monitoring covers only the submit error rate and email bounce rate. It has no alert owner, no defined action on breach, and nothing for the recent-signers or CDN path.
attacks.evidence: Watch `sign_submit_error_rate` (< 0.5%) and confirmation email bounce rate (< 2%) for 24h.

attacks.claim: Postmark processes EU signers' emails, but no transfer mechanism or processing location is stated beyond the DPA. Residency routing by postal code is not explained for unresolved or cross-border codes.
attacks.evidence: Confirmation emails go through Postmark; DPA countersigned 2026-09-14
